patch.value: Intent reads that tip over budget only with receipts settle in universal row compaction, which yields fewer rows per page than the overhead-charged intent pass on session-bounded reads

Found in the Codex review of PR #1758 (the pm-gh1753 fix). An intent read can tip over its budget only once the read-output receipts join the envelope. pm-gh1753's estimate mirror now settles such a page in the universal read-output compaction. That compaction drops rows and adds continuation metadata (output_budget_truncation, an output cursor), which itself costs room. Before the fix, the same page went through the intent layer's overhead-charged second pass, reached by the receipt-digit drift. That pass shrank the intent page and only rebased the cheaper producer next_cursor. Codex's repro: a TOON triage read with outputBudget 1000 and 1,309 tokens left in its output session. The six-row intent page measures 1,001 with receipts. The release that pm-gh1753 fixed returned five rows at 910 tokens; the fix returns three rows plus an output cursor, and with the session's remaining budget, following that cursor yields a budget omission. No row is lost: every row stays reachable through the cursor, in a new session if needed. But the first page yields fewer rows, and the session reaches fewer rows. Choosing the cheaper strategy deliberately, rather than by accident, is the work: try the overhead-charged intent projection before accepting a universally compacted intent page, and keep whichever delivers more rows within both ceilings. Cursors must stay bound to the first pass's uncompacted prefix (pm-gh1753's binding).

For an intent read whose settled envelope exceeds the intent budget only through read-output receipts, the delivered page is the candidate with more rows among the overhead-charged intent projection and the universally compacted page, both within the intent and session ceilings; Output cursors of either candidate replay against unchanged rows (the pm-gh1753 binding), and the 1,476-configuration replay harness stays at zero stale cursors; A spec reproduces the session-bounded triage case (outputBudget 1000, 1,309 session tokens left) and delivers at least the prior five rows

An intent page that exceeds its budget only once receipts are included is delivered by whichever compaction (overhead-charged intent pass or universal row compaction) keeps more rows within both the intent and session ceilings, with output cursors bound to the first pass's uncompacted prefix.
The universal compaction always settles it: Codex's session-bounded triage repro delivers three rows plus an output cursor where the prior release delivered five rows at 910 tokens.

value.text: Narrowed by PR #1758: the refusal variant is fixed there. A page the read-output stage would refuse outright is now decided again with the receipts' overhead charged to the intent pass (chargedIntentPassOrRefusal, recorded on pm-gh1753). What remains here is the yield preference: when universal compaction does deliver rows, but fewer than the overhead-charged intent pass would, still choose the pass that keeps more rows.
